nodes.eff: Free and unlocked at the start. The four branches open from here.
nodes.why: Cost 0 so the first year already offers four directions.

nodes.eff: City level cap 2 → 3.
nodes.note: Needs a level cap that doesn't exist yet. Today cities auto-grow to 10.
nodes.trade: Cities at level 3+ cost 1 more sustainability a year. Sprawl turns land into roads, and spread-out towns burn more per person.

nodes.eff: Every city at level 3+ earns +1 research a year on top of its level income.
nodes.why: Makes the city line feed the other three branches faster.
nodes.trade: Each city at level 3+ pays 3 money a year to run its university.

nodes.eff: Cities at level 3+: money −2 → +3 a year.
nodes.trade: Cities at level 3+: −1 sustainability a year. More trade means more goods made, shipped and thrown away.

nodes.eff: Cities at level 3+: +0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: Happiness runs 0–100 and a blackout costs 0.5 per missing unit of energy, so +0.5 per city sits on the same scale.
nodes.trade: Cities at level 3+ use 1 more energy (−8 → −9). City life runs on electricity.

nodes.eff: City level cap 3 → 5.
nodes.note: Your draft connects all three tier-2 nodes into this. Proposed: any one of them, so the tier is a choice, not a toll.
nodes.trade: Cities at level 5+: −1 happiness a year from crowding, until Hygiene Investments or Entertainment is researched.

nodes.eff: City population +5 → +7 a year.
nodes.why: Sewers and clean water drove most of the 19th-century gain in life expectancy.
nodes.note: There's no mortality in the model, so "reduce mortality" is read as faster growth.
nodes.trade: Sewers and water works: −2 money per city a year. In exchange it clears the crowding penalty from City Development 2.

nodes.eff: City level cap 5 → 7. Cities at level 6+ use one less energy (−8 → −7). Population boost
nodes.why: Dense cities use less energy per person: shared walls, shorter trips, district heating.
nodes.note: Empty in your draft; this is a suggested effect.
nodes.trade: Cities at level 6+: −0.5 happiness a year. High-rise living is efficient but not loved.

nodes.eff: City energy −8 → −6.
nodes.why: Buildings use about a third of the world's final energy; insulation, heat pumps and LEDs cut that sharply. Gives the city line its own answer to energy pressure besides building another plant.

nodes.eff: City sustainability −1 → 0.
nodes.why: Transport is the largest emitting sector in many countries; rail and buses move people at a fraction of the energy of cars.

nodes.eff: A city next to at least one forest earns +1 sustainability and +0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: Ebenezer Howard's 1898 Garden City. Introduces hex adjacency and makes forests worth keeping beside towns.

nodes.eff: City level cap 7 → 10. Cities at level 8+ earn +1 sustainability a year.
nodes.why: Paolo Soleri's whole-city-in-one-structure. The solarpunk capstone of the city line.

nodes.eff: Research per city level 1 → 1.5 a year.
nodes.trade: Labs need funding: −10 money a year.

nodes.eff: Gate: opens Biomass and Geothermal.
nodes.why: Carnot, 1824, and the steam engine. Burning something to boil water is the oldest way to make power, so this is the cheap first science.

nodes.eff: Gate: opens Wind Turbines and Atomic Physics.
nodes.why: Faraday's dynamo, 1831, turns any spinning shaft into electricity. Wind power needs a generator, not just a sail, and the study of the electron leads on to atomic physics.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Biomass.
nodes.why: Wood was the fuel for millennia, and burning it in a boiler needs nothing newer than Thermodynamics. That makes it the first new plant of a run, and its −1 sustainability makes it a stopgap, not a solution.
nodes.note: Split from your "… Nuclear, solar and biomass". Biomass is pre-industrial and nuclear needs 20th-century physics, so they now sit two tiers and ~150 years apart.
nodes.trade: Each Biomass plant fells its nearest forest every 20 years, until Sustainable Biomass. Fuelwood demand is a real driver of deforestation, and this ties biomass to the forest clock.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Geothermal: mountain only, E +20, S +1, M −4, $900.
nodes.why: Larderello, Italy, made the first geothermal electricity in 1904, but it takes deep drilling, so it also needs Oil Extraction. The physics is old; the expense is the rig.
nodes.trade: Drilling can trigger small earthquakes: each plant has a 2% chance a year of −3 happiness. A geothermal project in Basel was shut down after a 2006 quake.

nodes.eff: Biomass next to a forest: sustainability −1 → +1.
nodes.why: Biomass is only carbon-neutral if the forest regrows what's burned.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Wind. On a mountain: +20% energy, +20% build cost.
nodes.why: James Blyth lit his cottage with a wind turbine in 1887, once generators existed. The mountain bonus is the doc's "mais vento, mais custo": one TerrainBonus entry, the mechanism the coal mine already uses.
nodes.trade: Wind next to a city: −0.5 happiness a year (noise, the view). Community Energy turns this into +0.5.

nodes.eff: Wind can be built on the coast, +25% energy there.
nodes.why: The first offshore farm was Vindeby, 1991. Offshore turbines run at roughly 40–50% capacity factor against 25–35% onshore. Competes with Tidal for coast hexes.

nodes.eff: Gate: opens Nuclear Fission and Semiconductors.
nodes.why: Radioactivity (1896), the electron, quantum theory: one body of physics produced both the reactor and the solar cell. Its price is what pushes both into the second half of a run.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Nuclear and the uranium extraction it needs. But it's still dangerous
nodes.why: Fission was discovered in 1938 and the first grid reactor ran in 1954. It needs atomic physics and industrial-scale mining for uranium, hence Mechanized Mining.
nodes.note: Split from your "… Nuclear, solar and biomass". Also closes the TODO on Nuclear's requiredFuel in TileDataFactory.
nodes.trade: Fear: each Nuclear plant −1 happiness a year, plus the accident risk (see "Nuclear catastrophe odds"). Gen IV Reactors remove the fear.

nodes.eff: Gate: opens Solar and Computing.
nodes.why: Becquerel saw the photovoltaic effect in 1839, but a useful solar cell had to wait for doped silicon a century later. Computing comes from the same transistor.

nodes.eff: Uranium extraction sustainability −1 → 0. Nuclear no longer costs happiness.
nodes.why: Passive-safety designs cool themselves without power or operators; breeders get far more energy from the same uranium. The doc says nuclear is clean but not perceived as clean; this node is how the perception changes.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Solar.
nodes.why: Bell Labs' 1954 silicon cell reached 6% efficiency and was priced for satellites. Solar arrives late and expensive; Cheap Solar is what turns it into the backbone.
nodes.note: Solar should start crappy and evolve

nodes.eff: All research income +25%.
nodes.why: The transistor (1947) made computers, and computers made science faster.
nodes.trade: Data centres: −3 energy a year. They use 1–2% of the world's electricity.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Fusion: E +120, S 0, M −25, $5000, no fuel.
nodes.why: The capstone, priced to land around year 200–250 in a strong run: a reward for surviving, not a way out of the midgame. Plasma control is a computing problem, hence Computing.

nodes.eff: Solar build cost $250 → $150.
nodes.why: Swanson's law: module prices fall about 20% with every doubling of shipped capacity, close to 90% between 2010 and 2020.

nodes.eff: Wind and solar output swings are halved.
nodes.why: Numerical weather prediction is what lets real grids schedule wind and solar a day ahead.

nodes.eff: Every city makes +2 energy.
nodes.why: Shrinks the city's −8 without spending a plant hex, which matters on a crowded island.

nodes.eff: Stored energy cap 50 → 150.
nodes.why: Pumped hydro, from the 1890s, still holds over 90% of the world's grid storage.
nodes.note: Today surplus energy never gets lost, so this needs a cap first. See "Storage needs a ceiling" below.
nodes.trade: Energy put into storage comes back 20% smaller. Real pumped hydro returns 70–85%.

nodes.eff: Hydroelectric energy +40 → +48.
nodes.why: Modern Francis and Kaplan turbines convert over 90% of the water's energy.
nodes.trade: Bigger reservoirs: each Hydroelectric plant −1 sustainability a year. Flooded valleys rot and release methane.

nodes.eff: Coal Thermal energy +10 → +12. The triad goes from +2 to +4 energy.
nodes.why: Supercritical boilers raised coal plant efficiency from about 33% to about 42%.
nodes.trade: Each coal plant −0.5 happiness a year. Bigger boilers, more smog over town.

nodes.eff: Energy above the storage cap sells for $1 each instead of being lost.
nodes.trade: −0.5 happiness in any year you export. Selling power abroad raises prices at home.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Tidal.
nodes.trade: Barrages silt up the estuary behind them: Tidal sustainability +2 → +1. La Rance, the first big tidal plant, changed its estuary for good.

nodes.eff: Stored energy cap 150 → 500.
nodes.why: Lithium-ion grid battery costs fell about 90% between 2010 and 2023.
nodes.trade: Batteries need lithium: −1 sustainability a year. Brine mining drinks scarce water in dry regions.

nodes.eff: Coal Thermal energy +12 → +14.
nodes.why: Ultra-supercritical plants pass 45% efficiency. Each upgrade makes coal more tempting and leaves its −3 sustainability alone.
nodes.trade: Coal Thermal upkeep −3 → −5. Ultra-supercritical boilers need expensive alloys.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Oil Extraction (one well) and the Oil plant.
nodes.note: Closes the TODO on Petróleo's requiredFuel in TileDataFactory.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Gas Extraction and a Gas plant: E +30, S −2, M −6, $700.
nodes.why: Gas emits roughly half the CO₂ of coal per kWh, the "bridge fuel".
nodes.note: Needs FuelType.Gas and two new tile assets.
nodes.trade: Methane leaks: each Gas Extraction costs 1 more sustainability a year. Over 20 years methane traps about 80 times more heat than CO₂.

nodes.eff: Gas extraction money ×1.5, but each well costs 1 more sustainability and 0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: A deliberate temptation. Shale gas turned the US into a gas exporter, with groundwater and induced-quake costs.
nodes.trade: Each gas well −1 sustainability and −0.5 happiness a year.

nodes.eff: Oil plant energy +35 → +42.
nodes.note: Empty in your draft; this is a suggested effect.

nodes.eff: Oil extraction money +8 → +25.
nodes.note: Read as: the first wells barely pay until this is researched ("making it viable").

nodes.eff: Removes the one-well limit on oil extraction.
Coal sustainability −3 → −2, Oil −6 → −5.
nodes.why: Scrubbers and precipitators remove sulfur and soot, not CO₂, so the gain is real but small.
nodes.note: Hangs off Oil Energy in your draft; proposed to cover coal too.

nodes.eff: Fossil plant sustainability penalties halved, but their energy −20%.
nodes.why: Capture stores about 90% of a plant's CO₂ but spends 15–30% of its output doing it.
nodes.trade: Fossil plants lose 20% of their energy.

nodes.eff: Demolishing a fossil plant or extraction refunds 50% of its build cost and gives +3 happiness.
nodes.why: Rewards retiring coal on purpose, the story the game is named after.

nodes.eff: Each oil extraction +10 money a year.
Each oil extraction +0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: Plastics, medicine, fertiliser: the products are why oil was loved before it was feared.

nodes.eff: Oil extraction sustainability −2 → −1. Oil-spill events can no longer fire.
nodes.note: The event half waits on random yearly events, which aren't built.

nodes.eff: All plants +10% energy. Wind and solar swings removed.
nodes.why: Long-distance HVDC lines and demand response let a grid share surplus instead of curtailing it.

nodes.eff: Gas and Oil plants can run on hydrogen: no fuel needed, sustainability penalty 0, upkeep +50%.
nodes.why: Electrolysis turns surplus renewable power into fuel; it's how existing turbines get decarbonised.
nodes.trade: Hydrogen plants cost 50% more to run.

nodes.eff: All build costs −10%.
nodes.note: Empty in your draft. Proposed as the gateway to industry and, through it, environmental science.
nodes.trade: Industry pollutes: −1 sustainability a year, permanently. The first tradeoff on offer, in year 1.

nodes.eff: Power plant build costs a further −15%.
nodes.trade: Embodied carbon: every new building costs 5 sustainability once. Cement alone makes about 8% of the world's CO₂.

nodes.eff: Coal extraction money +20 → +26 (+24 → +31 on a mountain).
nodes.why: Mechanisation multiplied output per miner. Another temptation: coal pays better, drains the same.
nodes.trade: Each coal mine −0.5 happiness a year. Machines replace miners.

nodes.eff: The HUD shows the year sustainability runs out at the current rate.
nodes.why: Climate models made collapse visible decades before it arrived. Information is a legitimate research reward.
nodes.trade: Climate anxiety: −0.5 happiness a year while sustainability is below 500. In a 2021 survey of 10,000 young people, 59% were very or extremely worried about climate change.

nodes.eff: Territory can be bought: new coast hexes on the island edge, price rising each time.
nodes.why: Dutch polders. Closes the doc's "compra direta com $" expansion.

nodes.eff: Demolishing any tile refunds an extra 25%.
City money −2 → +2. Demolition refunds in full.
Plant a forest on an empty open hex for $150. It counts as forest after 10 years.
nodes.why: Felled forest is the real clock on a run (+3 S each). This turns it from a stock you only spend into one you can rebuild.

nodes.eff: Forests +3 → +4 sustainability.
nodes.trade: Protected forests cost $400 to fell instead of $200.

nodes.eff: Every 25 years, each forest seeds one empty neighbouring open hex.
nodes.why: Natural regeneration is often cheaper and richer than planting.

nodes.eff: Each forest +2 money a year.
nodes.why: Makes standing forest pay, the opposite of the $200 felling fee.

nodes.eff: Nuclear energy is now safer for the people, the odds of nuclear catastrophe reduces in 50%
nodes.trade: Safety staff and inspections: −2 money per Nuclear plant a year.

nodes.eff: The chances of nuclear catastrophe is now  1 in a million
nodes.trade: Another −2 money per Nuclear plant a year.
More ore processed: each uranium extraction costs 1 more sustainability a year.

nodes.eff: Now your country produces nuclear war power
nodes.note: New reandom effects will be unlocked
nodes.trade: −1 happiness a year, and bad events tied to weapons become possible.
Deeper wells: the earthquake chance per Geothermal plant rises from 2% to 5% a year.
Stadiums and screens: each city uses 1 more energy.

nodes.eff: Each Hydroelectric plant adds +100 to the stored energy cap.
nodes.why: Pump water uphill when power is spare, let it fall when it's needed. Built since the 1890s, it still holds over 90% of the world's grid storage. Ties storage to the waterfall hexes instead of making it a flat number.

nodes.eff: Unlocks Wave: coast only, E +10, S +2, M −5, $600. Cheaper and weaker than Tidal, so a coast hex has three uses to choose between.
nodes.why: Still close to experimental in reality (Pelamis 2008, Mutriku 2011), so it belongs late and pricey. It gives the coast more competition with Tidal and Offshore Wind.

nodes.eff: Each Wind or Solar plant next to a city gives +0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: Danish wind co-ops: by around 2000 more than 100,000 households owned shares in turbines, and local ownership is the strongest predictor of people accepting turbines near them. Rewards building clean energy beside towns, not just anywhere.

nodes.eff: Cities +1 sustainability a year, but each uses 2 more energy (−8 → −10).
nodes.why: Electric motors are about three times as efficient as engines, but electrifying transport moves its fuel demand onto the grid. A real tradeoff: only worth it if your grid is clean.
nodes.trade: Each city uses 2 more energy.

nodes.eff: Every plant +5% energy (transmission losses gone). Suggested as an extra requirement for Fusion.
nodes.why: Grids lose roughly 5–8% of their power in the wires. High-temperature superconductors (1986) carry current with no loss, and the same magnets made compact fusion reactors credible (MIT/CFS's 20-tesla magnet, 2021).
nodes.trade: Cryogenic cooling: −2 money per plant a year.

nodes.eff: Solar energy 10 → 15. Pairs with your "start crappy and evolve": Solar opens at 6, Better Solar takes it to 10, this to 15.
nodes.why: Real cell efficiency went 6% (Bell Labs, 1954), ~15% (commercial silicon, 2000s), ~22% (today's panels), and perovskite-on-silicon tandems passed 33% in the lab in 2023. Three steps match three eras.

nodes.eff: Nuclear plants stop costing sustainability for spent fuel (suggested base: −1 a year per plant until this is researched).
nodes.why: Spent fuel stays dangerous for millennia. Finland's Onkalo, bored 400 m into bedrock, is the first permanent repository, starting in the mid-2020s. Gives the nuclear line a cost to pay down besides accidents.

nodes.eff: Each fossil plant and extraction −3 money a year; every city +0.5 happiness a year.
nodes.why: Sweden has taxed carbon since 1991; its emissions fell by about a third while the economy kept growing. The first policy node: it makes fossil fuel cost what it does, and the player chooses when to pay that.
nodes.trade: Every fossil plant and extraction pays 3 money a year.

nodes.eff: Wind, Solar, Tidal and Wave build costs −25%.
nodes.why: Germany's 2000 renewable energy law guaranteed a price for clean power. It made Germany the world's biggest solar market for a decade, and that demand helped drive panel prices down for everyone.
nodes.trade: Subsidies: −2 money per clean plant a year. Germany's renewable surcharge raised household bills for two decades.

nodes.eff: Demolishing an extraction lets you replant the hex as forest for $50; it counts as forest at once.
nodes.why: The US has required mined land to be restored since 1977. Gives every coal mine a planned end, and lets the player turn the most damaged hexes back into the forest that keeps a run alive.

nodes.eff: Every trade-off from the CITY branch have 70% of chance to be ignored

decisions.body: Your draft gates tidal, solar, nuclear, biomass and oil behind research. Today all nine are in the build menu from year 0. Proposed start palette: City, Coal Extraction, Coal Thermal, Hydro. Wind wasn't in the draft, so it's proposed under Research.
decisions.src: TileDefinition needs a requiredResearch field; BuildPanel hides locked tiles.

decisions.body: "Energy can now be stored and won't be lost" has nothing to fix today: surplus energy piles up with no cap. The doc also says storage is implicit in ⚡. Proposal: a base cap of 50, Energy Storage 150, Better Storage 500, and surplus above the cap is lost until Energy Exports sells it.
decisions.src: ResourceManager clamps energy at 0 only. Changes doc §Decisões "Storage".

decisions.body: "Upgrade your city up to level 3" implies a cap. Today auto-growth reaches level 10 with no research. Proposal: base cap 2, then 3, 5, 7, 10 along the city line. Since level only buys research, the cap throttles research early, which paces the whole tree.
decisions.src: CityGrowth needs a max-level read from ResearchManager.

decisions.body: City Development 2 and Hygiene hang off University, Trade Market and Urbanization together. ResearchNode prerequisites are all-of, so as drawn you'd have to buy all three. Proposal: any one of the three, which turns the tier into a choice.
Oil Tracking "lets you open more than one oil extraction", so oil starts limited to one well. Coal has no such limit. Fine as an oil-specific rule, but it's a new kind of rule: a per-tile count cap.
decisions.src: TileDefinition needs maxCount, lifted by a research flag.

decisions.body: Coal Power and Coal Power 2 take a thermal plant from +10 to +14 energy. One city's −8 then needs 0.57 plants instead of 0.8, so per city the coal drain falls. Upgrading coal is a sustainability gain until you spend the surplus on growth. That's a good trap; just make sure it's intended.

At 1 point per city level per year, a run averaging 12 levels on the board earns about 3,600 by year 300; with Research, Computing and University stacked, closer to 7,000. Against the tree total above, a strong run buys roughly half to two-thirds of the tree. Is that the share you want?
decisions.src: Costs are placeholders on a 20 → 1200 curve. ResearchManager.pointsPerCityLevel = 1.

decisions.body: Nodes tagged "system" need a mechanic first: wind/solar intermittency (doc §3, not modelled), random events (Safe Oil), hex adjacency (Garden City, Sustainable Biomass), nuclear's happiness penalty (doc says it, code doesn't), territory purchase (Coastal Engineering).
decisions.src: These are the expensive nodes to build. Everything else is data.

decisions.body: Nuclear Security I and II need a base rate to cut. Real reactors have had about three major accidents in roughly 20,000 reactor-years, about 1 in 7,000 per plant per year: too rare to ever happen in a 300-year run. A game rate has to be much higher to be felt. Suggestion: 0.5% per plant per year (about 40% over a century), 0.25% after Security I, 0.01% after Security II. A meltdown destroys the plant, closes the hex for 30 years, and costs about −100 sustainability and −30 happiness.
decisions.src: Needs the random-events system. Risk shown in the build tooltip so it's a choice, not a surprise.

decisions.t: Tradeoffs that switch on at a city level
decisions.body: City Development, City Development 2, Trade Market, Urbanization and Verticalization now charge a cost only for cities above a level. That brings back some level dependence, which BalanceTests guards against for the city's own effect. These are research modifiers on top of the constant city row, not a level multiplier, but the test (or the rule in CLAUDE.md) should say which of the two it protects.
decisions.src: BalanceTests asserts the city's per-turn effect is the same at every level.
